result.title: Two for One: Privileged Learning for Resource-Constrained Screening
result.summary: Machine learning systems are often developed under data-rich conditions but deployed when only incomplete information is available. A natural example arises in colour fundus photography (CFP), where both eyes are commonly imaged because they can provide complementary information for ocular disease assessment. Prior approaches that exploit bilateral information either fuse both eyes in a single model or use knowledge distillation to compress a dual-eye teacher into a lightweight student that still requires both images at test time. However, bilateral acquisition may not always be feasible. We thus propose a privileged learning framework in which a teacher model has access to bilateral CFP images during training and learns representations informed by information from both eyes, while the student is trained to transfer this knowledge from the bilateral teacher using only a single-eye image as input. At inference, the student operates exclusively on this single-eye input and does not require the contralateral image. Experimental results show consistent improvements in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve over conventional monocular training, with the largest gains observed for left-eye images for the detection of age-related macular degeneration (0.931 vs. 0.966) and diabetic retinopathy (0.789 vs. 0.836).%, while requiring only a single-eye image at inference. By enabling models to benefit from bilateral information during training while requiring only a single-eye image at inference, our approach may support more reliable deployment in resource-constrained clinical and screening environments.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种特权学习框架：训练时教师模型可访问双眼眼底图像并学到融合双侧信息的表示，学生模型仅以单眼图像为输入通过蒸馏传递该知识，推理时无需对侧图像；在 AMD 与糖尿病视网膜病变检测上 AUC 稳定优于常规单眼训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 「训练期可用、推理期不可得的额外视觉证据被蒸馏进单输入模型」这一非对称信息设置，可供核查其是否能为 LVR 中把视觉证据压入内部状态、以及视觉旁路与信息坍缩问题提供训练监督线索；但原文属医学图像分类，不涉及推理轨迹或 latent 状态生成，迁移仅为可能。
